claims.summary: The descendant defines "consent," "deep fake," and "depicted individual" for deep fakes of any individual; the origin's section has no such definitions.
The descendant bars willful dissemination of a deep fake without the depicted individual's written consent, with injunctive relief, actual and punitive damages, costs, and attorney's fees.
The origin makes the sponsor of an electioneering communication liable, and a medium liable only if it removes a required disclosure or alters content into synthetic media.
The descendant lists exemptions for parody with disclosure, news broadcasts, paid broadcasts, publications, research, and legal proceedings, and keeps 47 U.S.C. 230 immunities intact.
The descendant defines "deep fake," "consent" and "depicted individual," covering realistic, technically produced media lacking adequate labeling or disclaimers.
The descendant makes it unlawful to knowingly disseminate a deep fake without the depicted person's written consent, with injunctive relief, actual and punitive damages, costs and attorney fees.

The origin limits liability for electioneering communications to the sponsor, making a medium liable only if it strips the disclosure or alters content into synthetic media; the descendant lacks this.
The origin lets an interactive computer service be held liable when it strips disclosures or alters content; the descendant bars such liability, preserves 47 U.S.C. 230, and exempts news media.
